newsitem.title: ITALY: Ssangyong plans Italian auto venture.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong plans Italian auto venture.

text.p: South Korea's Ssangyong Motors has signed a letter of intent with Italian auto distributor Gruppo Vignuzzi to create a joint venture which will assemble up to 30,000 four-wheel drive vehicles in Italy, newspapers reported.
The reports, carried by most Italian newspapers, said that initially Ssang Yong would acquire 15 percent of the venture and Vignuzzi would take 10 percent.
The venture would invest some $100 million in the plant, creating 800 jobs.

State industrial company Gepi and Spi, an offshoot of state industrial holding group Iri, would respectively acquire 24 and 25 percent of the venture. The balance of the new company was likely to be bought up by Italian banks.
Milan business daily Il Sole said that Ssangyong would probably be able to raise its stake to 49 percent within five years.
Il Sole carried a statement signed by Italy's Transport Minister Claudio Burlando on a trip to Seoul saying the government would assist the venture in identifying an appropriate manufacturing site.
The government would also "examine favourably the possibility of helping the initiative by granting all the financial assistance currently available under Italian and European law."
Three sites are currently under consideration -- one in the north-eastern port of Genoa, one further down the coast at Massa Carrara and a site in the southern port of Gioia Tauro.
Output from the plant would be targeted at the public sector, including the police, the ambulance service and the fire brigade. -- Milan newsroom +392-66102321
